title: [Upgrade] Live upgrade modules skip RemovesUpgrades except ObjectCreation/SubObjects
description:
## C++
`giveSelfUpgrade` (UpgradeModule.cpp:140-147) calls `processUpgradeRemoval` **before** `upgradeImplementation`. `UpgradeMuxData::muxDataProcessUpgradeRemoval` (Module.cpp:226-244) looks up each `RemovesUpgrades` name and `obj->removeUpgrade(template)` so mutually exclusive upgrades (bomb-truck payloads, etc.) reset.

## Rust
Only `ObjectCreationUpgrade` and `SubObjectsUpgrade` parse `RemovesUpgrades` and call `process_upgrade_removal`. All other live object/upgrade modules have no removal list and `apply_upgrade` never strips conflicting upgrades.

## Evidence
C++ Module.cpp:226-244. Rust leftover.rs upgrade_factories parse_from_ini without RemovesUpgrades. subobjects_upgrade.rs:157-158 and object_creation.rs:201-202 do process removals.

## Player-visible effect
Switching an exclusive upgrade (e.g. bomb-truck payload / conflicting object upgrades) leaves the previous upgrade executed; both stay on.

title: Align Main path-grid cells to CPP absolute world coordinates
description:
## Evidence
Main PathfindingGrid::new_with_origin stores origin = GameLogic.world_min; world_to_grid currently casts (world - origin) / 10 and grid_to_world reconstructs origin + index * 10 (GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/game_logic/pathfinding/grid_core.rs:177-190). GameLogic initializes symmetric extents such as world_min = -world_width/2 (game_logic/construct.rs:38,530), which need not be a multiple of the 10-unit path cell size. For extent min -256, Rust maps world x=0 to relative cell 25, while CPP absolute cell 0 with map origin -26 corresponds to storage index 26. The Rust cell lattice is shifted by 4 world units versus CPP.

## Regression
Use a non-cell-aligned world extent (e.g. -256), place one obstacle at the CPP absolute-world-derived storage cell, and compare Rust world-to-cell, adjusted route waypoint, and blocker avoidance against worldToGrid + m_xOrigin + adjustCoordToCell. Include negative coordinates and exact map edge. Preserve truncation toward zero and CPP separately rounded path extent.

## Limits
This is source-grounded coordinate arithmetic; a live Main route differential is still needed. It is adjacent to, but distinct from, the loaded terrain/classification ownership issue in hq-i10n6.

title: [Display] Gamma ramp stored but never applied to the frame
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::setGamma` (`W3DDisplay.cpp` 519-524) calls `DX8Wrapper::Set_Gamma(gamma, bright, contrast, calibrate)` in fullscreen (windowed returns so desktop gamma is untouched). `W3DDisplay::init` applies `TheGlobalData->m_displayGamma` when != 1. ## Rust
`Display::set_gamma` / Options `apply_options` / `apply_display_gamma` only write `display_fx::GAMMA_STATE` (`display.rs` 547-548, `menu_callbacks.rs` 1058-1072). `apply_gamma_pass` (`display_fx.rs` 346-363) is a no-op (`let _ = (encoder, device, ...);` comment about a future pass) and is never called. `apply_gamma_rgba` / `gamma_uniform` have no live render callers (tests only). title: [GameClient] IME never hooks OS input or opens candidate window
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GUI/IMEManager.cpp` `IMEManager::serviceIMEMessage` handles Win32 `WM_IME_*` via IMM32 (`ImmGetContext` / `ImmGetCompositionStringW`). On `IMN_OPENCANDIDATE` it calls `openCandidateList`, which loads `IMECandidateWindow.wnd` and fills the candidate listbox. Composition chars are sent to the attached text-entry as `GWM_IME_CHAR`. `GadgetTextEntrySystem` (`GadgetTextEntry.cpp`) attaches `TheIMEManager` on focus and detaches on blur. `enable()` calls `ImmAssociateContext`.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/ime_manager.rs` `ImeManager::service_ime_message` only mutates in-memory `ImeMessage` enum state. `attach()` stores a `Weak` pointer and never associates an OS IME context. `enable()`/`disable()` flip a bool. There is no `openCandidateList` that creates `IMECandidateWindow.wnd`. Candidate gadgets are only clicked by residual `simulate_*` / `drive_os_wnd_*` test helpers. `src/gui/gadgets/text.rs` has `ime_composition` fields labeled "placeholder for IME" and never calls `get_ime_manager().attach`.

## Evidence
Rust `service_ime_message` match arms update `composition_string` / `candidates` only; they never `winSendInputMsg(..., GWM_IME_CHAR, ...)`. C++ `GadgetTextEntryInput` ignores keys while IME is composing; Rust text-entry never consults the IME manager.

## Player-visible effect
CJK / IME users cannot compose or pick candidates in chat, login, or other text fields. Candidate window never appears. Only Latin keyboard input works.
